ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, for the rhombus $ABCD$ with side length $AB=2\sqrt{3}+2$ and $\angle ABC=60^\circ$, two points $E$ and $H$ are taken on the diagonal $BD$ such that $BE=DH$ and $AE\parallel FH$. When $\angle AED=75^\circ$, what is the sum $AE+FH$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct FM$\perp$BD at M, EN$\perp$AB at N. \\
Because quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus and $\angle$ABC=$60^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle$ABD=$\angle$ADB=$30^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle$AED=$75^\circ$=$\angle$ABE+$\angle$BAE, \\
it results in $\angle$BAE=$45^\circ$, \\
Given $\angle$ENA=$90^\circ$, \\
it leads to $\angle$NAE=$\angle$NEA=$45^\circ$, \\
hence NA=NE, \\
Let NA=NE=x, then BE=2x, and BN=$ \sqrt{3}$x, \\
Since AB=2$ \sqrt{3}$+2, \\
it implies that $ \sqrt{3}$x+x=2$ \sqrt{3}$+2, \\
thus x=2, \\
Therefore, BE=4, AE=2$ \sqrt{2}$, \\
Since $\angle$HFD=$180^\circ$−$\angle$FHD−$\angle$FDH=$75^\circ$ and $\angle$FHD=$75^\circ$, \\
it concludes that $\angle$DFH=$\angle$DHF, \\
Therefore, DF=DH=BE=2, \\
In the right triangle $\triangle$FMD, \\
since $\angle$FMD=$90^\circ$ and $\angle$FDM=$30^\circ$ with DF=4, \\
it follows that FM=2, DM=2$ \sqrt{3}$, and HM=4−2$ \sqrt{3}$, \\
therefore, FH=$ \sqrt{FM^{2}+HM^{2}}$ \\
=$ \sqrt{2^{2}+(4−2\sqrt{3})^{2}}$ \\
=2$ \sqrt{6}$−2$ \sqrt{2}$, \\
Thus, AE+FH=2$ \sqrt{6}$−2$ \sqrt{2}+2$ $\sqrt{2}$ \\
=$\boxed{2 \sqrt{6}}$.

Reasoning: Let the side length s=2√3+2. Establish a coordinate system according to the figure, take B=(0,0), D=(s√3,0). Because ∠ABC=60° and BD is the diagonal of the rhombus, BD bisects this angle, A is below BD, so A=(s√3/2,-s/2). Let E=(t,0). Since ED is along the positive x direction, and ∠AED=75°, there is tan75°=(s/2)/(s√3/2-t). Therefore t=s√3/2-s/(2tan75°). Also tan75°=2+√3, so cot75°=2-√3, obtaining t=s(√3-1)=2(√3+1)(√3-1)=4. Therefore BE=4, and AE=√[(s√3/2-4)^2+(s/2)^2]=√[(√3-1)^2+(√3+1)^2]=2√2. From BE=DH, obtain H=(s√3-4,0)=(2+2√3,0). Vector EA=A-E=(√3-1,-√3-1). Let F be on AD, F=A+λ(D-A), and at the same time FH is parallel to AE, so F=H+μ(√3-1,-√3-1). Substitute A=(3+√3,-√3-1), D-A=(3+√3,√3+1). From the y-coordinate obtain -1+λ=-μ, that is μ=1-λ; from the x-coordinate obtain (3+√3)(1+λ)=2+2√3+μ(√3-1). Solving simultaneously obtains λ=2-√3, μ=√3-1. Therefore FH=μ·|EA|=(√3-1)·2√2=2√6-2√2. Thus AE+FH=2√2+(2√6-2√2)=2√6.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/vector route. First read the diagram as a rhombus with diagonal BD drawn horizontally from B to D, A below the diagonal, C above it, E and H on BD with E left of H, and F on side AD with FH drawn parallel to AE. From the text use AB=s=2√3+2, ∠ABC=60°, BE=DH, AE∥FH, and ∠AED=75°. Place B=(0,0), D=(s√3,0), because in a 60° rhombus the diagonal BD bisects the angle at B and triangle ABD has base angle 30°. Then A=(s√3/2,-s/2). Let E=(t,0). Since ED is the positive x-direction and ∠AED=75°, impose tan75°=(s/2)/(s√3/2-t), giving t=BE=4 and AE=2√2. Then H=(s√3-4,0). Find F as the intersection of side AD with the line through H parallel to vector EA. Parametrize AD and the parallel line, solve the two linear equations, and obtain FH=2√6-2√2. Add AE+FH to get 2√6.

推理：由菱形 ABCD 且 ∠ABC=60°，对角线 BD 平分 B、D 两角，所以 ∠ABE=30°，∠HDF=30°。因为 E 在 BD 上，EB 与 ED 是反向射线，而 ∠AED=75°，所以 ∠AEB=180°-75°=105°。在三角形 ABE 中，三个角为 30°、105°、45°，即 ∠BAE=45°。

用正弦定理：AB=2√3+2=2(√3+1)。
BE/ sin45° = AB/ sin105°，所以 BE=(2√3+2)·sin45°/sin105°=4。
AE/ sin30° = AB/ sin105°，所以 AE=(2√3+2)·sin30°/sin105°=2√2。

题设 BE=DH，因此 DH=4。又 FH∥AE，HD 与 ED 同向，所以 ∠DHF=∠AED=75°。在三角形 DHF 中，∠HDF=30°，∠DHF=75°，因此 ∠DFH=75°，从而 DF=DH=4。

再用正弦定理：FH/DH=sin30°/sin75°，所以 FH=4·sin30°/sin75°=2/sin75°。由于 sin75°=(√6+√2)/4，FH=8/(√6+√2)=2√6-2√2。

因此 AE+FH=2√2+(2√6-2√2)=2√6。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, for the rhombus $ABCD$ with side length $AB=2\sqrt{3}+2$ and $\angle ABC=60^\circ$, two points $E$ and $H$ are taken on the diagonal $BD$ such that $BE=DH$ and $AE\parallel FH$. When $\angle AED=75^\circ$, what is the sum $AE+FH$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct FM$\perp$BD at M, EN$\perp$AB at N. \\
Because quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus and $\angle$ABC=$60^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle$ABD=$\angle$ADB=$30^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle$AED=$75^\circ$=$\angle$ABE+$\angle$BAE, \\
it results in $\angle$BAE=$45^\circ$, \\
Given $\angle$ENA=$90^\circ$, \\
it leads to $\angle$NAE=$\angle$NEA=$45^\circ$, \\
hence NA=NE, \\
Let NA=NE=x, then BE=2x, and BN=$ \sqrt{3}$x, \\
Since AB=2$ \sqrt{3}$+2, \\
it implies that $ \sqrt{3}$x+x=2$ \sqrt{3}$+2, \\
thus x=2, \\
Therefore, BE=4, AE=2$ \sqrt{2}$, \\
Since $\angle$HFD=$180^\circ$−$\angle$FHD−$\angle$FDH=$75^\circ$ and $\angle$FHD=$75^\circ$, \\
it concludes that $\angle$DFH=$\angle$DHF, \\
Therefore, DF=DH=BE=2, \\
In the right triangle $\triangle$FMD, \\
since $\angle$FMD=$90^\circ$ and $\angle$FDM=$30^\circ$ with DF=4, \\
it follows that FM=2, DM=2$ \sqrt{3}$, and HM=4−2$ \sqrt{3}$, \\
therefore, FH=$ \sqrt{FM^{2}+HM^{2}}$ \\
=$ \sqrt{2^{2}+(4−2\sqrt{3})^{2}}$ \\
=2$ \sqrt{6}$−2$ \sqrt{2}$, \\
Thus, AE+FH=2$ \sqrt{6}$−2$ \sqrt{2}+2$ $\sqrt{2}$ \\
=$\boxed{2 \sqrt{6}}$.

it follows that $\angle$ABD=$\angle$ADB=$30^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle$AED=$75^\circ$=$\angle$ABE+$\angle$BAE, \\
it results in $\angle$BAE=$45^\circ$, \\
Given $\angle$ENA=$90^\circ$, \\
it leads to $\angle$NAE=$\angle$NEA=$45^\circ$, \\
hence NA=NE, \\
Let NA=NE=x, then BE=2x, and BN=$ \sqrt{3}$x, \\
Since AB=2$ \sqrt{3}$+2, \\
it implies that $ \sqrt{3}$x+x=2$ \sqrt{3}$+2, \\
thus x=2, \\
Therefore, BE=4, AE=2$ \sqrt{2}$, \\
Since $\angle$HFD=$180^\circ$−$\angle$FHD−$\angle$FDH=$75^\circ$ and $\angle$FHD=$75^\circ$, \\
it concludes that $\angle$DFH=$\angle$DHF, \\
Therefore, DF=DH=BE=2, \\
In the right triangle $\triangle$FMD, \\
since $\angle$FMD=$90^\circ$ and $\angle$FDM=$30^\circ$ with DF=4, \\
it follows that FM=2, DM=2$ \sqrt{3}$, and HM=4−2$ \sqrt{3}$, \\
therefore, FH=$ \sqrt{FM^{2}+HM^{2}}$ \\
=$ \sqrt{2^{2}+(4−2\sqrt{3})^{2}}$ \\
=2$ \sqrt{6}$−2$ \sqrt{2}$, \\
Thus, AE+FH=2$ \sqrt{6}$−2$ \sqrt{2}+2$ $\sqrt{2}$ \\
=$\boxed{2 \sqrt{6}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rhombus ABCD, B is on the left, D is on the right, and diagonal BD is horizontal; C is above BD, A is below BD; E and H are on BD and E is to the left of H; F is on side AD, and segments AE and FH are drawn as mutually parallel oblique lines. Reasoning: Let the side length s=2√3+2. Establish a coordinate system according to the figure, take B=(0,0), D=(s√3,0). Because ∠ABC=60° and BD is the diagonal of the rhombus, BD bisects this angle, A is below BD, so A=(s√3/2,-s/2). Let E=(t,0). Since ED is along the positive x direction, and ∠AED=75°, there is tan75°=(s/2)/(s√3/2-t). Therefore t=s√3/2-s/(2tan75°). Also tan75°=2+√3, so cot75°=2-√3, obtaining t=s(√3-1)=2(√3+1)(√3-1)=4. Therefore BE=4, and AE=√[(s√3/2-4)^2+(s/2)^2]=√[(√3-1)^2+(√3+1)^2]=2√2. From BE=DH, obtain H=(s√3-4,0)=(2+2√3,0). Vector EA=A-E=(√3-1,-√3-1). Let F be on AD, F=A+λ(D-A), and at the same time FH is parallel to AE, so F=H+μ(√3-1,-√3-1). Substitute A=(3+√3,-√3-1), D-A=(3+√3,√3+1). From the y-coordinate obtain -1+λ=-μ, that is μ=1-λ; from the x-coordinate obtain (3+√3)(1+λ)=2+2√3+μ(√3-1). Solving simultaneously obtains λ=2-√3, μ=√3-1. Therefore FH=μ·|EA|=(√3-1)·2√2=2√6-2√2. Thus AE+FH=2√2+(2√6-2√2)=2√6.
